headline: CPI Day Arrives as Iran Tensions Cloud the Pre-Market Mood
body_html:
Wall Street futures face a cautious open on Wednesday after U.S. equities slipped Tuesday as hopes for a U.S.-Iran diplomatic breakthrough evaporated. Overnight, European bourses held largely flat, with traders opting to stand aside ahead of July's consumer-price index — the single most consequential data point of the week. The dollar edged higher in Asian hours as geopolitical unease kept haven demand alive, while oil pushed further into positive territory on mounting doubts that any deal in the Strait of Hormuz is near.

The inflation print itself is expected to show a moderate monthly increase, with easing gasoline prices acting as a partial offset. Markets will be parsing the details closely: a cooler-than-forecast reading could revive rate-cut speculation, while any upside surprise risks tightening financial conditions just as earnings season winds down. Shipping data showing Hormuz traffic falling to a one-week low underscores that the supply-side risk premium in oil has not dissipated.

Tuesday's session offered a mixed underlying picture — 316 issues in our universe advanced against 229 decliners — with homebuilders and semiconductors leading while consumer names lagged. Freight carrier Hub Group shed nearly 20% to stand as the session's sharpest casualty. Watch the 8:30 a.m. ET CPI release as the definitive tone-setter at the open.

briefs.headline: CPI Report Set to Dictate Wednesday's Direction
briefs.body: July consumer prices are forecast to have risen only modestly, helped by a pullback in gasoline costs. Traders will scrutinize the core reading with particular care; any deviation from expectations in either direction is likely to reprice rate-cut odds swiftly and set the early tone for equities and bonds alike.

briefs.headline: Oil Climbs as Iran Deal Optimism Continues to Unravel
briefs.body: Crude extended gains overnight after diplomatic hopes surrounding the Strait of Hormuz failed to solidify. Hormuz shipping traffic dropped to its lowest level in a week amid ongoing hostilities, and a U.S. military strike on a vessel in the Gulf of Oman reinforced concerns about near-term supply disruptions, keeping an elevated risk premium baked into energy prices.

briefs.headline: Hub Group Collapses Nearly 20% in Heaviest Single-Stock Blow
briefs.body: Freight operator Hub Group was Tuesday's most punishing decliner, tumbling 19.75% in a session that otherwise showed reasonable breadth. The move dragged on the broader industrials complex, which managed only a fractional gain of 0.27% for the day, masking significant dispersion within the sector between engineering and equipment names.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor-Equipment Names Power Higher on Strong Session
briefs.body: Onto Innovation surged 9.76% and FormFactor climbed 7.65% on Tuesday, helping lift the semiconductors sector to a 1.45% gain — second-best among all groups tracked. The twin advances suggest ongoing confidence in capital-equipment spending cycles, an area investors will continue to monitor as chip-demand forecasts are updated through the back half of 2026.

briefs.headline: Red Sea Violence Intensifies; Crew and Rescuers Reported Killed
briefs.body: A fresh attack in the Red Sea claimed four crew members and two rescuers, adding to a grim toll of maritime incidents in the region. The incident, coupled with the U.S. strike in the Gulf of Oman, underscores that trade-route risk remains acute and could feed through to freight rates and insurance costs in the weeks ahead.

briefs.headline: Cardinal Health Price Target Lifted After Bullish Profit Guidance
briefs.body: Analysts raised their price target on Cardinal Health following the healthcare distributor's upbeat profit outlook. The upgrade offers a bright spot within a healthcare sector that finished Tuesday essentially flat, down just 0.02%, and may attract fresh attention to the segment if Wednesday's CPI data does not materially disturb the broader risk tone at the open.
